rules.condition: When the clocking element has several clocking items
rules.statement: Exactly one clocking item dictionary should have the boolean field primary set to true.

rules.condition: For blocks that generate clocks or resets
rules.statement: The clock and reset fields of a clocking item are optional.
The primary clock clocking item must have both clock and reset fields.
Special care will be required for security sensitive storage elements.
Security storage elements should be handled with care regardless of reset methodology, since they might leak sensitive state content.
Care may include synchronously resetting the value after chip-wide reset to a randomized value.
Asynchronous active low reset incurs slightly more area and needs more hand-holding but is more common.
Synchronous active high reset is slightly more efficient but requires a clock edge to take effect.
Peripherals can connect to the chip bus.
Every peripheral must expose at least one device interface on the chip bus.
Peripherals can act as a bus host, though the preferred model is the processor being primary host.
The bus_interfaces attribute in the configuration file should contain a list of dictionaries describing the interfaces the peripheral exposes.
The peripheral must have a protocol of tlul.
Each bus_interfaces entry must contain a direction, which must be either host or device.
All bus hosts must use the same clock as the defined primary host clock.

rules.condition: When another entry in the list has the same direction
rules.statement: An entry must include a name so port names do not collide.

rules.condition: Where possible, except inherited IP too tricky to convert
rules.statement: All interrupts shall have common naming, hardware interfaces, and software interfaces.
All lowRISC peripheral designs must conform to the register specification.

rules.condition: For each item name in the interrupt list
rules.statement: The module must have an output named intr_name_o for each interrupt name.
The name key, a string naming the interrupt, is required.
The desc key, a string describing the interrupt, is optional.
The type key is optional, selecting Event or Status, defaulting to Event if unspecified.
Wired CIP interrupts use active-high level-triggering.
A peripheral generates a separate wired interrupt for each interrupt source.
INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE and INTR_TEST registers are created at offsets 0x0, 0x4, 0x8 with one bitfield per interrupt.
The .hjson must not define more than 32 interrupts per peripheral.
INTR_ENABLE enables/masks the output of INTR_STATE to create the wired interrupt signal intr_o.
INTR_TEST is write-only and asserts the interrupt for testing.
INTR_STATE is not qualified by INTR_ENABLE and shows the raw state of latched hardware interrupt events.
The current interrupt can only be cleared by handler acknowledgement, a W1C write to INTR_STATE.
The event is latched into its INTR_STATE bitfield and intr_o goes high; a software W1C write clears it and intr_o goes low.
